marks.gloss_en: ולא ביחיד בזמן שאין ברגלו מכה -- הא יש ברגלו מכה נפיק: the mishna's condition implies its converse
אלמא קסבר סנדל לשום צער עביד -- since he shods the wounded foot, the sandal is for pain
hence, if there is a wound on his foot, he goes out [in a single sandal]
אלמא קסבר לשום תענוג עביד -- since he shods the healthy foot, the sandal is for comfort
Chiyya bar Rav: he goes out [with the sandal] on the [foot] that has no wound
דאמר ליה רבי יוחנן לרב שמן בר אבא: הב לי מסנאי; יהב ליה דימין; אמר ליה: עשיתו מכה -- the shod foot counts as the wounded one, as Rav Huna (kind svara under protest: an incident adduced as proof)
and R' Yochanan too holds this [view] of Rav Huna
ודילמא כחייא בר רב סבירא ליה, והכי קאמר: עשית של שמאל מכה -- perhaps he holds as Chiyya bar Rav and meant: you have made the LEFT [unshod] foot a wound
ואזדא רבי יוחנן לטעמיה -- being handed the right shoe first was a fault because, for him, shoes begin on the left
כתפילין כך מנעלין: מה תפילין בשמאל אף מנעלין בשמאל
R' Yochanan: as tefillin, so shoes
סך ראשו תחילה, מפני שהוא מלך על כל איבריו
when he washes, he washes the right and afterwards the left
מיתיבי: כשהוא נועל -- נועל של ימין ואחר כך נועל של שמאל -- the baraita has the right first, against R' Yochanan
the baraita: when he puts on [shoes], he puts on the right and afterwards puts on the left
השתא דתניא הכי ואמר רבי יוחנן הכי, דעבד הכי עבד ודעבד הכי עבד -- both practices are valid (= p_rav_yosef_dabad_hachi). Abaye's challenge to this reply (61a.8) cannot be attached to it; see header
Rav Yosef: now that it is taught so and R' Yochanan said so, whoever did this did [rightly] and whoever did that did [rightly]
when he removes [them], he removes the left and afterwards the right
Abaye: perhaps R' Yochanan had not heard this mishna [baraita], and had he heard it he would have retracted
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: a God-fearing person fulfils both
דיקא נמי, דקתני ולא בקמיע בזמן שאינו מן המומחה, ולא קתני בזמן שאינו מומחה. שמע מינה -- the mishna speaks of the writer's expertise, not the amulet's
the mishna: nor [may one go out] with an amulet when it is not from an expert
the Tosefta: what is a proven amulet? any that healed, and again, and a third time
the Tosefta: not [only for] one who has been seized [by the falling sickness], but [also] so that he not be seized
the Tosefta: and he ties and unties [the amulet] even in the public domain
דילמא אתי לאיתויי ברשות הרבים -- the prohibition rests on the fear of carrying, so it holds whatever one says of tefillin on Shabbat
the mishna: nor [may a man go out on Shabbat] with tefillin
מאי טעמא? דרך מלבוש עבידא -- going out in them is wearing, not carrying, so no sin-offering whatever one holds about tefillin on Shabbat
the mishna: and if he went out [with tefillin] he is not liable to a sin-offering
